title: Images gained motion, and the model shelf grew
summary:
New media models landed while usage, checkout, and API-key behavior became easier to inspect and less likely to fail for the wrong reason.

Wan 2.6 was added as `wan` for 720p image-to-video clips lasting 2–15 seconds, with optional auto-dubbed audio. `klein-large` brought 9B image generation and reference-image editing under a non-commercial license, while `gemini-legacy` added Gemini 2.5 Pro with a 1M-token context window and multimodal inputs. Image work also clarified z-image output limits and aligned Klein editing requests around query parameters and JSON arrays of reference images.

Enter gained daily graphs for requests and Pollen spending, with time ranges, API-key and model filters, and CSV exports. A daily usage API returns breakdowns by date, model, and billing source. Account profiles gained `nextResetAt` for the next daily Pollen reset, and apps gained `GET /api/account/key` to check a key’s expiry, permissions, budget, and rate-limit status without generating anything.

Pollen pack checkout moved through Polar before Stripe replaced it on the pack buttons later in the week. Stripe checkout was added for $5, $10, $20, and $50 packs, with promotion codes, tax handling, VAT IDs, and invoices; existing crypto balances were preserved when crypto purchases were removed. Insufficient Pollen and exhausted key budgets now return HTTP 402, leaving 403 for access denied.

Image requests without a model parameter use the default again. Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Opus 4.5 fallbacks supply the `max_tokens` value Vertex AI requires, and Claude fallbacks convert remote image URLs for Vertex AI and Bedrock. API-key verification was raised to 10,000 requests per second; rate limits now return 429 rather than resembling invalid keys. Model Monitor also separates billing and access errors from model health.
